title: Longest Common Subsequence
prompt:
Return the length of the longest subsequence (characters in order, not necessarily contiguous) common to `text1` and `text2`.

**Example**: `"abcde"`, `"ace"` → `3`.

The canonical 2-D DP — the pattern lesson's template code IS this problem.
hints: (m+1) x (n+1) table; dp[i][j] = LCS of the first i chars of text1 and first j of text2.
Chars match (`text1.charAt(i-1) == text2.charAt(j-1)`) → extend the diagonal: dp[i-1][j-1] + 1.
No match → best of dropping one char from either side: max(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]).

solution.explanation: O(m·n). Row/column 0 stay 0 (LCS with an empty string), which the +1 sizing gives for free. This table is the parent of Edit Distance and many other string DPs — same skeleton, different cell rule.
